resources.title: Change in a local area
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 28 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a forty-minute lesson about change in a local area for three to four pupils. Use an invented town with a high street, a park and a bus route. Pupils compare one then-and-now pair and share a change privately through speech, pointing, their usual aid or directed scribing.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!B43/C43: Talk about how my local area has changed. Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

Week 4 is formative. The owner sets Week 6 as assessing. Success is a matched place pair and one accurate then/now change, supported by two picture clues or a clearly identified known generic example. A same feature or possible effect is extension.

Set Source Cards pages 1–2, Support Cards page 1, the word mat, visible model and books at each place. Keep the full labelled picture key. Adult may cut pairs along white gaps and mark then/now and place type on the reverse. Pupils may point to the whole sheet.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Level 2 describes the requested scaffolds, not a qualification level. Supported, Independent and Aspire retain all supports. Exact scribing and usual communication aids are available. No public questioning, cold calling or required reading aloud.

All pictured places and changes are invented. They are teaching examples of places that can be in a local area, not records of a pupil’s actual area. A pupil may use a change they already know, described by type only, but this is optional. Never request names, addresses, directions or personal home details. Record model example or pupil-stated example; do not turn a model response into a verified local-history claim.
Change in a local area continued
Thursday 28 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes match park views and find the tree in both. Keep bank, stem and model visible.
5 minutes source teaching with brief reset; 5 minutes park model and private hinge; 5 minutes guided high street or bus-stop comparison.
10 minutes private sharing and book record with brief reset; 3 minutes private check and response; 2 minutes exit and evidence.

“A local area has places near us. This town is made up. It helps us practise talking about change. I match the same place. Then there was no bench. Now there is a bench.” Point to both park views. “You can choose words, point or ask me to write.”

Offer added/taken away: “What happened to the bench?” Added. If unsure, trace the space in the then view and the bench in the now view. Parallel check: shelter added or taken away? Added. Keep the visible model. Do not ask for a public answer or remove supports to test memory.

Work from pictures in the room. No visit, live map or online research is needed. Adult cuts cards if wanted. Touch is optional. Offer HELP/PASS, a quiet request, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause. Pupils can stay with the invented example without explaining why.

Pupil selects a pair, points to both clues and chooses a change statement. Adult writes exact words or selected labels, reads back quietly and offers keep/change. Record actual prompts, source of the ideas and response mode. Copying alone does not establish a communicated comparison.
Change in a local area continued
Thursday 28 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: choose a pair and two labels, then direct an exact scribe. Independent: share and keep one paired then/now statement with all scaffolds. Aspire: add one same feature or a possible effect using the bank, stem and model. Every route communicates one change.

Cognition: one pair and one step at a time. Communication: quiet wait time, usual aid and exact scribe; plan in any language. SEMH: predictable steps, optional personal example and private help. Sensory/physical: large pictures, adult cutting and optional touch. Words, shape, position and borders carry meaning without colour.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W04-E1: chosen place type, then/now statement, two clues, model or known-example basis and actual help. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil; absent pupils stay blank. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode precede R. E follows actual banking. No actual results are pre-filled.

A local maintenance worker notices what has changed and what needs care. Offer authentic pupil words or choices to the Communication portfolio. Do not infer independent speech, reading, writing or award completion from supported communication.

resources.title: Staff answers and support
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 28 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Talk about how my local area has changed. From BUILD Weekly - Spring!B43/C43. Thursday 28 January 2027, P3. Theme: Resilience & Change. Formative; Week 6 is assessing under the owner brief.

Top row then; bottom row now. Left high street: steps replaced by a ramp; shop fronts remain. Middle park: a bench added; tree and path remain. Right stop on a bus route: shelter added; pole and fence remain. Starter: the park pair both show the tree. Accept another accurate visible feature if linked to both views.

All scenes and changes are invented teaching examples. No real place, street, building, maker or date is identified. The label then/now is supplied context. Bus times, fares, route length and reasons for change are unknown. Do not infer them from the shelter picture.

Define local area as places near us and use the model town to practise change language. An optional already-known example can be described by type only, such as a park or bus stop. Never ask for names, addresses, routes home or personal details. Record pupil-stated experience separately from the invented model. Do not invent an actual local change to fill a gap.

A changed feature does not mean the whole place is new. Match the same tree/path or shop fronts before comparing. Bench added or removed? Added. Parallel check: shelter added or removed? Added. Reteach by pointing to the space then and new feature now. A possible effect is not proof of why a change happened.
Thursday 28 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Use the fourth pupil-number field only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Record each pupil’s own selection and communicated then/now change. A shared model alone does not establish an individual response.

Every task keeps bank, starters and visible model. Read labels quietly if wanted. Scribe exact words or selected labels and read back for keep/change. Record who supplied the ideas and actual prompts. No public questioning or required reading aloud. Talk may use speech, pointing or usual aid.

One same feature: the tree remains. A possible effect: a bench may help people rest; a shelter may help people stay dry. These are possible uses, not verified reasons or views held by everyone. Word bank: same, tree, bench, rest, may. Starter: The __ is still here. A __ may help us __. Model: The tree is still here. A bench may help us rest.

Use HUM-BUILD-S1-W04-E1. Offer authentic responses to the Communication portfolio. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s own response precede R. Actual banking precedes E. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks remain separate; no qualification completion is inferred.

image.alt: Six invented town scenes in three matched then-and-now pairs. Top earlier, bottom later. Left high street steps become a ramp; middle park gains a bench; right bus stop gains a shelter. Shop fronts, park tree/path and stop pole/fence remain. No real place, building or historical date is represented.

slides.notes:
HUM-BUILD-S1-W04 · Year A · Thursday 28 January 2027 · P3
A change in the park: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Model the park comparison. Then there was no bench. Now there is a bench. Point to the same tree and path to match the place. Quiet hinge: was the bench added or taken away? Added. If unsure, trace then without bench and now with bench, keeping word bank and model. Parallel check: was the bus shelter added or taken away? Added. No public question.
Outcome verbatim: Talk about how my local area has changed.

slides.notes:
HUM-BUILD-S1-W04 · Year A · Thursday 28 January 2027 · P3
My change talk: 10 minutes.
Teacher: At minute 25 include a short reset within this ten-minute block. Choose a model pair and share one change privately, then keep the selected words or picture record in a book. A pupil may offer an already-known change in their own area using type words only, with no names or directions; there is no requirement to disclose. Record its basis and any uncertainty. Supported: select two labels and direct an exact scribe. Independent: form the paired statement with all supports. Aspire: add a same feature or a possible effect, marked may.
Outcome verbatim: Talk about how my local area has changed.

My quiet check: 3 minutes.
Teacher: Private review. Pupil points to the two clues or confirms a known generic example. Exact scribe reads back for keep/change. Separate what is visible from what might happen. Adult support brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Hidden adult brief: Level 2 means bank, starter and visible model every task, not a qualification level. Prompt ladder: point, short private prompt, rephrase, choice/scaffold, model first step then return task. Invented town examples are not verified personal local history.
